Thought: When caustics (strong bases) are mixed with non-oxidizing acids, several reactions can occur. Let me analyze each option:

A. Explosion - This is typically associated with oxidizing reactions, not simple acid-base reactions.
B. Fire - Acid-base reactions don't typically cause fire directly.
C. Flammable gas generation - Some acid-base reactions can generate hydrogen gas, which is flammable.
D. Heat generation - Acid-base neutralization reactions are exothermic and release heat.
E. Innocuous and non-flammable gas generation - Some acid-base reactions can produce non-harmful gases.
F. May be hazardous but unknown - This is too vague.
G. Solubilization of toxic substance - This could happen in specific cases but isn't a general outcome.
H. Toxic gas generation - Some acid-base reactions can produce toxic gases.
I. Violent polymerization - This is more associated with organic chemistry reactions, not typical acid-base reactions.

The primary and most consistent reaction when caustics mix with non-oxidizing acids is an exothermic neutralization reaction, which generates heat (option D). In some specific cases, depending on the exact chemicals involved, gas generation (options C, E, or H) might occur, but heat generation is the universal outcome.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
